question: Separate finite-pool density error, learned-score fitting error, and smoothing-induced loss of useful boundary direction, before any closed-loop adaptation.
fixed: archived initial classifier and source-only coordinates
archived query points, normals and pair orientation
baseline sigma from the original 512 inputs when varying N
architecture 64-64 SiLU, float64 CPU, Adam lr=0.001, batch 128
400 optimizer updates, 51200 sample presentations, identical initialization and exact Gaussian noise tensors across settings

pool_protocol.baseline: original target512 from E1/E2 archive; exact tensor prefix
pool_protocol.extension: sample_gmm(7680, dim, seed+9100), transform with frozen source coordinates; nested prefixes 2048 and8192
pool_protocol.baseline_schedule: production seed+102 randperm and training noise stream replayed exactly
pool_protocol.larger_pool_schedule: separate seed+9102 shuffle stream, without replacement each epoch; stop at400 updates
pool_protocol.validation_noise: original seed+103 on original512 inputs, evaluated every4 updates in all settings

checkpoints.secondary: lowest same-pool independent-noise DSM loss over100 checks; save selected state and update
checkpoints.historical_baseline_audit: secondary baseline must reproduce archived production checkpoint bitwise; historical baseline primary may differ in d2
checkpoints.saved: initial/final/selected states, Adam state, per-update loss, every validation loss, exact batch IDs and noise tensors

queries.source: exact E1/E2 queries.pt, stripping old score arrays only; never regenerated or reprojected
primary: auxiliary_planes raw x1=-0.5,+0.5 with512 nuisance inputs each
queries.note: baseline noisy query sets are fixed locations, not draws from each new smoothed law; auxiliary nuisance coordinates come from original target pool, no independent-query generalization claim

normal_queries: two sign counts and recalls, balanced sign accuracy
signed clipped-request RMSE in sigma and raw units
oracle/estimate normal signal magnitude, clipping fraction, displacement toward raw target boundary0
metrics.sign_masks: legacy per-reference abs(sigma*gamma)>1e-3, plus common population-eligible intersection across0.5/1/2 sigma; report denominators; do not invent balanced scores if a sign absent
metrics.geometry: boundary displacement is -zeta*n; desired gamma sign is sign(raw_x1*n_x1)
metrics.aggregation: five-seed mean and sample SD, every seed retained; paired setting-minus-baseline differences; no best-setting selection or claim of statistical significance

interpretation: lower learned-vs-empirical error concerns fitting; empirical-vs-population concerns finite pool; both are descriptive, not additive scalar RMSE decomposition
bandwidth changes the oracle itself; inspect correct-direction fraction as well as estimation accuracy
for symmetric means +/-1 and raw variance0.25, smoothing can merge peaks; population accuracy alone is insufficient
fixed400 updates isolates sample pool effect at fixed compute; it cannot rule out gains with more training
static directional diagnostics alone do not establish adaptation BA/NLL improvement

progression_screen.purpose: descriptive gate for considering a later closed-loop run, not target-label model selection or a theorem
criteria: learned normal RMSE and signed-request RMSE below zero-score baseline on initial and auxiliary queries
auxiliary balanced sign accuracy above0.5 and both sign recalls above0.5
population and learned directions point toward target0, not a smoothing-induced central density peak
consistent in at least4/5 paired seeds; all outcomes reported
progression_screen.decision: report and wait for user decision; do not execute closed loop

records: fixed inputs/query hashes and immutable classifier
all score checkpoints and optimizer states
scalar tables, figures, audit and failure records
full nonoverwriting tar.gz with member hash verification
archiving.github: report, code, scalar tables, figures, logs and manifests; no tensor/checkpoint binaries

label_policy: No real data or target evaluation labels. Synthetic component IDs generated internally for sampling are discarded; training/selection uses only unlabeled inputs and noise.
